Imagine paying house rent for 25 years. Your children have grown up, you are approaching retirement, and you are still worried about the next rent increase.

This is the reality for many hardworking Nigerians.

When I embarked on my economic reforms in 2023, expanding access to affordable, long-term credit was a priority.

That is why we established the ₦1 trillion MOFI Real Estate Investment Fund (MREIF) @mreifng.

Through this initiative, eligible Nigerians can now access mortgages of up to ₦100 million at a fixed interest rate of 9.75%, with up to 20 years to repay and an initial deposit of just 10%.

What does this mean for you?

If you want to buy a ₦10 million house, you can make an initial deposit of ₦1 million and repay about ₦85,400 monthly over 20 years.

Already, over 2,300 Nigerians across 27 states have accessed ₦160 billion in mortgages through MREIF alone.

We have also strengthened the Federal Mortgage Bank of Nigeria (FMBN), where eligible Nigerians can access housing loans of up to ₦50 million at 6% interest, with up to 30 years to repay.

If you have a pension account, you may also qualify to access up to 25% of your retirement savings towards your initial deposit. If you are married, you can submit a joint application with your spouse, increasing your chances of accessing a higher amount.

For Nigerians who cannot afford a mortgage, Family Homes Fund @fhfl_ng supports the delivery of affordable housing, with more than 53 social homes delivered for vulnerable and underserved households. 

Our Renewed Hope Social Housing Programme also targets 77,400 affordable homes across the country. We have already delivered 100 free homes to widows in Kaduna and another 50 to the wives of our fallen heroes in Ibadan.

Across Nigeria, over 15,000 homes are also under construction through our Renewed Hope Cities and Estates Programme.
You should not need to know a minister, a governor or anybody in the Presidential Villa to apply and benefit from these opportunities.

These programmes are for Nigerians who meet the requirements, wherever they live and whatever their beliefs.
 
As President, I take particular satisfaction in seeing hardworking Nigerians become homeowners and families gain the security that comes with having a place of their own.

That, too, is what my economic reforms are about.

From Reforms to Opportunities.

Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR
President

BREAKING: Texas A&M’s $205.5 million semiconductor project will help train America’s next generation of chipmakers for Terafab. 🇺🇸

University leaders say Terafab’s planned chip plant in Grimes County makes A&M’s Semiconductor Institute even more relevant, with Terafab counting on the institute to help attract talent. 

• $205.5 million project: The institute’s new building in Bryan and supporting water infrastructure will serve chip research, development and workforce training. 

• Practical training for Terafab jobs: Director Steve Putna says students will train in an environment designed to help them move smoothly into Terafab’s workforce.

• Access to engineering talent: Texas A&M graduates more than 5,000 engineers annually, giving nearby chipmakers a major source of potential recruits.

• Industry-style facilities: The institute will feature a cleanroom and six laboratories, giving students practical experience with semiconductor technology.

• Construction is progressing: The building is about 20% complete. Substantial completion is expected by the end of 2027, with significant operations planned for mid-2028. 

• Infrastructure for long-term growth: Regents just approved $14.2 million for a new well and storage system supporting the RELLIS campus, including the institute.
